extra.message: The 'search' request argument is read from request.args.get('search', '') and interpolated directly into an f-string SQL query: s_query = f"SELECT filename FROM files WHERE user_id = {user_id} AND filename LIKE '%{search_query}%'", which is then passed to cursor.execute(s_query). An attacker can inject SQL via the search parameter (e.g. ' UNION SELECT password FROM users--), enabling data exfiltration and authentication bypass. Use a parameterized query instead.

The dashboard search box renders the user-controlled search_query with the Jinja2 '| safe' filter: value="{{ search_query | safe }}". search_query comes from request.args.get('search', '') in server/routes.py:126 and is reflected unescaped, allowing reflected XSS (e.g. ?search="><script>alert(1)</script>). Remove '| safe' or escape the value.

The user's country is rendered with the Jinja2 '| safe' filter:

Country: {{ user.country | safe}}

. country is attacker-controlled at signup (server/routes.py:83) and update_profile (server/routes.py:186) and persisted in the database, so a stored XSS payload is executed whenever the profile is viewed. Remove '| safe' to restore auto-escaping.

The comment input value is concatenated into HTML and appended to the DOM without sanitization: $commentList.append('
  • ' + comment + '
    • '); where comment comes from the user-controlled text input. This is a DOM-based XSS sink; a payload such as executes. Use .text() or sanitize the input.

The /api/v1/update_picture endpoint takes a user-supplied 'picture_url' from the request payload and fetches it server-side with requests.get(picture_url) (line 254) without any allow-list or SSRF protection. An attacker can force the server to make requests to internal services / cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), and the fetched bytes are then written to a web-accessible path (lines 282-285).

Broken Object Level Authorization: the /api/v1/profile endpoint is unauthenticated (the @token_required decorator is commented out at lines 152-153) and returns any user's record selected solely by the client-supplied user_id query parameter (SELECT username, email, country, role, permissions, team FROM users WHERE id = ?). Any anonymous caller can enumerate user_id to read every user's PII, role and permissions.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Broken Function Level Authorization: the DELETE /api/v1/delete-user/<int:user_id> endpoint has its @token_required decorator commented out (lines 221-222) and performs no authentication or authorization check before executing DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ? (line 232). Any unauthenticated attacker can delete arbitrary users by ID.

The POST /api/v1/update_picture endpoint is completely unauthenticated (no token_required and no session check). It accepts an arbitrary 'username' in the body and updates that user's profile_picture (lines 266-288), so any anonymous attacker can modify any user's profile picture and trigger server-side requests.

Broken Object Property Level Authorization / privilege escalation: the /update_profile handler trusts client-supplied 'role' and 'permissions' form fields (role = request.form['role'] or current_user['role']; permissions = request.form['permissions']) even though they are hidden in edit_profile.html, and writes them directly in the UPDATE at lines 229-234. Any authenticated user can POST role=admin&permissions=all to grant themselves administrative privileges.

Path traversal / unrestricted upload: the /upload handler uses the raw client-supplied filename (filename = file.filename) with os.path.join(UPLOAD_FOLDER, filename) and file.save(filepath) without calling werkzeug.utils.secure_filename. A multipart filename such as ../../server/config.py or ../../run.py escapes the uploads directory and overwrites arbitrary files on the server.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Unrestricted file upload: the /upload endpoint accepts any file type and size with no extension, MIME-type or content validation before saving it to the uploads directory and serving it back via /uploads/<filename> and /download/<filename>. An attacker can upload .html/.svg files containing JavaScript (stored XSS on the app origin) or other dangerous content.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (hashlib.md5(password.encode()).hexdigest()) in custom_hash, which is used for both signup and login (routes.py:50, 93) and in the API (api_v1.py:127). MD5 is cryptographically broken, unsalted and fast, enabling rainbow-table and brute-force attacks. Use a slow salted KDF such as bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 or werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: Hardcoded secret key: SECRET_KEY = "just_another_secret". This key signs Flask session cookies and the JWT tokens (api_v1.py:94, 133). Because it is a weak, publicly-committed constant, an attacker can forge session cookies and valid HS256 JWTs, leading to authentication bypass and privilege escalation. Load the secret from an environment variable or secret manager.

Insecure configuration: DEBUG = True is loaded into the Flask app (server/__init__.py:10) and passed to app.run(debug=debug_mode) in run.py:7-10. Running Flask with the debugger enabled in production exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger (potentially leading to code execution if the PIN is obtained) and leaks stack traces. Disable debug mode in production.

Weak session management: SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = False is applied at run.py:9, so the session_token cookie is readable from JavaScript and can be stolen via XSS. The app also sets no SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE or SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE, exposing the session to interception and CSRF. Enable HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite on session cookies.

Cross-Site Request Forgery: state-changing endpoints such as /update_profile (POST, routes.py:170), /upload (POST, routes.py:248) and /delete/<filename> (POST, routes.py:340) rely solely on the session cookie and include no CSRF token or SameSite protection. An attacker-controlled page can silently submit a form or POST request to change the victim's profile (including role), upload or delete files.

Sensitive data exposure via verbose error handling: the broad except block returns the raw exception text to the client with {'message': str(e)} (line 298). This leaks internal paths, network details and stack information that help an attacker. Return a generic error message and log the details server-side.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Lack of brute-force protection: the /login handler (and the API /api/v1/login at api_v1.py:110) performs password verification with no rate limiting, account lockout, CAPTCHA or delay. Combined with weak unsalted MD5 hashes, an attacker can perform unlimited online password-guessing against user accounts.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
